items.title: [science.org] Study estimates summer heat killed 50,391 in European cities
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

Researchers estimate that summer heat caused 50,391 excess deaths across 854 European cities in 2026, the highest toll in their records. They attributed 32,619 deaths to the additional warming caused by human-driven climate change. The study covers urban areas representing about 40% of the population in 30 countries; its authors say the total across Europe was likely higher because it excludes rural areas and a deadly May heatwave. The team from Imperial College London and the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine used city-level temperature records and historical links between heat and mortality to model deaths, then compared the observed heat with a climate-modeled scenario without human-caused warming. Heat deaths are often not recorded as such on death certificates, and the estimate is not a count of individually verified deaths. Researchers and public-health specialists have called for warning systems, accessible cooling, urban greening and support for vulnerable residents, alongside reduced fossil-fuel use.

items.title: [The Guardian Global Development] ‘For Panama, it is life or death’: how drought is choking the canal that feeds a nation
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

Failed rains and a dire El Niño threaten the waterway that sustains the country, with farmers selling cattle to survive

The cattle should be ambling, grazing contentedly, through Robert Delgado’s fields. Instead, the animals slump in the shade, tongues lolling, in futile attempts to avoid the blistering heat. Soon it will matter little whether their appetite returns, for there will be no grass left to graze.

In Azuero, an agricultural region in Panama’s Arco Seco (Dry Arc), the summer is generally relentless and unforgiving. But this year, the crucial rainy season that precedes it – typically from May to December – has brought little rain to parched fields. The watering holes, streams and rivers that farmers rely on have not been replenished, and pastures – the vital source of animal feed during the dry months – have not regenerated themselves.

items.title: [thehindu.com] Pacific waters top 30°C as El Niño tracks toward historic peak
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

The central Pacific's Niño 3.4 region passed 30°C for the first time in recorded history on Oct. 5, as scientists report record heat accompanying the developing El Niño, a natural climate pattern that alters rainfall and temperature worldwide. Surface temperatures there reached 30.06°C, and the anomaly rose to 3.48°C on Oct. 18 before easing to 3.34°C this week. NOAA's Climate Prediction Center puts the chance of a strong-to-very-strong event at 83%; the World Meteorological Organization projects a peak anomaly of 3.8°C around December. NASA satellite measurements, drawn from a 35-year record, show the current pattern resembles October 1997, with unusually high sea levels and warm water extending east toward South America.

items.title: [bleepingcomputer.com] Hackers weaponize LiteLLM release to steal credentials across systems
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

Hackers compromised the release pipeline for LiteLLM, an open-source AI gateway, and published version 1.107.0 containing credential-stealing malware on PyPI and Docker on Oct. 21. The malicious release affected Windows, Linux and macOS installations and targeted cloud, developer and AI-service credentials. The project says its private enterprise registry was not affected. LiteLLM said attackers used stolen GitHub CLI tokens to alter and trigger the release, apparently after accessing an internet-exposed internal deployment. It has not confirmed how they gained access. The compromised package has been removed. Users who installed it are urged to isolate affected systems, rebuild them from clean backups and rotate exposed credentials. Version 1.106.2 is the latest clean release.

Credential abuse: About four and a half hours after the data theft, Wiz observed attackers testing stolen AWS credentials and checking access to Amazon Bedrock models, consistent with attempts to hijack cloud-based AI services (helpnetsecurity.com, thehackernews.com). Exposure window: The malicious PyPI package was available from 11:39 to 13:23 UTC, while affected Docker tags served it until 14:20 UTC on Oct. 21 (helpnetsecurity.com, thehackernews.com). Data exfiltration: The malware encrypted stolen data with AES-256-CBC, protected the key with RSA-4096 and sent the data to litellm[.]dev/healthcheck (bleepingcomputer.com).

items.title: [livescience.com] Polar ice melt is making Earth’s solid surface rounder
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

Melting polar ice is making Earth’s solid surface rounder at an accelerating rate, according to research published in the journal JGR Solid Earth. Satellite-navigation measurements show that between 2011 and 2015, the poles rose and the equatorial bulge shrank by about 0.5 to 1 millimeter per year as ice loss eased pressure on the polar crust and meltwater added mass near the equator. The study examined the solid Earth. When ocean water is included, Earth as a whole is becoming flatter by about 0.8 millimeter a year because water accumulates toward the equator.

The company said its existing backup archives remained encrypted, isolated and preserved, with no indication they were compromised.

items.title: [theglobeandmail.com] Canadian military links grenade-range training to fire that killed four
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

A wildfire that killed four soldiers and injured 39 at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright began during routine training on an automatic grenade launcher range, Canadian military police said Thursday. The fire began inside a restricted danger area where firefighters could not attack it directly. A shift in wind direction and speed then drove the flames into another training area where soldiers were practising. As of Thursday, 27 injured members remained in hospital, including 13 in critical condition. Investigators have established the fire’s origin but are examining why it was not initially considered a threat and why live-fire training took place in the afternoon during a high-risk fire month. Wainwright’s range guidance recommends early-morning firing between August and October, and officials said they would review the decision to proceed. Military police, a military Board of Inquiry and Alberta’s Chief Medical Examiner are conducting separate investigations. The inquiry will examine training and safety procedures. Chief of the Defence Staff Gen. Jennie Carignan said interim safety changes would be made quickly if needed. The board’s findings will be made public when complete.

items.title: [Neuroscience News] How the Brain Maps Every Number
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

How does the human brain process abstract mathematical values? Brain scans from the INSERM-CEA Cognitive Neuroimaging Unit reveal a continuous spatial map in the intraparietal sulcus that plots fractions and whole integers along a single mental number line.
